claim: Rewarding Doubt (Bani-Harouni et al.) proposes a novel RL approach optimizing a log-scoring-rule reward whose optimal policy yields perfectly calibrated verbalized confidence expressions integrated into the generative process.
stance_target: RL reward shaping can train models to express calibrated confidence
quoted_support: The optimal policy under our reward design would result in perfectly calibrated confidence expressions.

claim: Models trained with the Rewarding Doubt reward generalize to unseen tasks without further fine-tuning, suggesting the emergence of a general confidence-awareness capability rather than task-specific overfitting.
stance_target: RL-trained confidence expression generalizes zero-shot to new domains
scope_conditions: unseen downstream tasks after single-domain RL training
quoted_support: Models trained with our approach exhibit substantially improved calibration and generalize to unseen tasks without further fine-tuning, suggesting the emergence of general confidence awareness.

claim: The Rewarding Doubt reward explicitly penalizes both over-confidence and under-confidence, distinguishing it from binary-correctness rewards that are indifferent to confidence miscalibration direction.
stance_target: reward must penalize both directions of miscalibration to induce calibration
quoted_support: Our method optimizes a reward based on the logarithmic scoring rule, explicitly penalizing both over- and under-confidence.
